attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing Yang-Mills theorem is the finite OS-matrix trace theorem for reflected Wilson products: as collars collapse to t=0, prove E(F)=0, or prove an invertible compatible congruence already locked into the observable renormalization. Existing RG compactness and single-loop convergence do not by themselves control mixed reflected cusp, hairpin, or contact terms.
steps: Fix a finite positive-time family F=(F_1,...,F_n) in the locked gauge-invariant algebra and choose collar representatives T_delta F_i supported a positive distance delta from the reflection plane.

At the regulated level, reflection positivity gives c^*M_{a,L,delta}(F)c >= 0 for all c in C^n. This is valid because the reflection plane separates Theta T_delta F_i from T_delta F_j and the lattice/regulated transfer-matrix positivity applies to the gauge-invariant algebra.
Use the RG-to-continuum topology at fixed delta to pass a,L to the continuum entrywise. Since the positive semidefinite cone in finite Hermitian matrices is closed, M_delta(F)>=0.
Assume the trace limit N(F)=lim_{delta downarrow 0}M_delta(F) exists entrywise. Again by finite-dimensional closedness, N(F)>=0.
If the trace theorem proves N(F)=M(F), then M(F)>=0 and OS positivity for this finite family follows immediately. This is the strict no-defect same-theory case.

More generally, if the trace theorem proves N(F)=R(F)^*M(F)R(F) with R(F) invertible and already induced by locked observable renormalization, then for any x choose y=R(F)^{-1}x; x^*M(F)x=y^*N(F)y>=0. Thus positivity transfers through an invertible congruence.

Now test why a merely positive collar limit is insufficient. Let M=[[1,2],[2,1]], which is not positive because it has eigenvalue -1. Let a pair-dependent boundary defect E=[[0,-2],[-2,0]], so N=M+E=I is positive. The collar theory would be OS-positive, but it gives no proof that the intended target M is positive. This model captures the logical risk of a nonfactorizing mixed Wilson cusp/contact defect.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is logically valid conditional on the trace/congruence hypothesis, but it does not establish the hypothesis for continuum four-dimensional Yang-Mills Wilson loops. In particular, it lacks a bound excluding pair-dependent boundary anomalies in S(Theta W(C_delta) · W(D_delta)).

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: finite OS-matrix boundary-defect factorization

assumptions: For each fixed delta>0 and finite family F, the cutoff matrices M_{a,L,delta}(F) with entries S_{a,L}(Theta T_delta F_i · T_delta F_j) are positive semidefinite.
The cutoff-removal topology is strong enough that M_{a,L,delta}(F) converges entrywise to M_delta(F) for every finite reflected collar family; hence M_delta(F) is positive semidefinite.
For the finite span V_F=span{F_1,...,F_n}, the trace limit N(F)=lim_{delta downarrow 0} M_delta(F) exists entrywise.

There is either no defect, N(F)=M(F), or a compatible invertible finite-span operator R(F) with N(F)=R(F)^*M(F)R(F). Compatibility means that passing to a subfamily restricts R(F), so the construction does not depend on an artificial enlargement of the test algebra.
definitions: source object: a net of cutoff/collar Schwinger functionals S_{a,L,delta} on a locked gauge-invariant positive-time test algebra, including Wilson loop observables T_delta F supported in t>=delta and satisfying lattice/reflection positivity before cutoff removal.

target object: continuum Schwinger distributions S on the same gauge-invariant observable algebra, with OS matrices M(F)_{ij}=S(Theta F_i · F_j) required to be positive semidefinite for all finite positive-time families.

controlled interface: RG convergence first at fixed collar delta for every reflected finite OS matrix entry, followed by a trace/collar limit delta downarrow 0 whose defect must be identified at the matrix level, not merely observable by observable.

same-theory condition: the collar trace map is the identity on the locked renormalized observables, or an already fixed invertible congruence coming from the same observable renormalization; no pair-dependent Wilson cusp, hairpin, or boundary-contact factor may be inserted after the target theory has been specified.

equations.label: finite OS matrix
equations.valid_when: F_i belong to the positive-time gauge-invariant test algebra and the reflected product is a valid Schwinger distributional pairing.

equations.label: collar positivity after RG limit
equations.valid_when: delta>0 is fixed and the RG topology controls every reflected collar matrix entry.

equations.label: trace defect decomposition
equations.valid_when: The collar trace limit exists; E(F)=0 is the strict same-theory case, while nonzero E(F) must be justified as an already locked renormalization rather than an added boundary theory.

equations.label: congruence-safe defect
equations.valid_when: The defect is induced by an invertible observable reparametrization compatible across all finite OS matrices.

equations.label: rank-one multiplicative Wilson-factor test
equations.valid_when: All relevant M_{ij} are nonzero and the suspected Wilson boundary anomaly is multiplicative; the displayed vanishing of all 2-by-2 minors is the finite-family test for B_{ij}=\overline z_i z_j, hence for a diagonal congruence.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Construct two positive-time Wilson observables F_1,F_2 for which the collar matrix N=lim_delta M_delta is positive but the intended target matrix M has a negative eigenvalue, with E=N-M not representable as R^*MR-M by any compatible locked renormalization. Such an example is a same-theory falsifier even though reflection positivity remains valid for the boundary-renormalized collar theory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates exactly what must be proved after the formal closed-cone step: not just convergence of single Wilson loops, but a finite OS-matrix no-defect or congruence-factorization theorem for mixed reflected Wilson products at the reflection plane.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite reflected Wilson-product boundary defects are harmless for OS positivity only when they are induced by an invertible congruence on the finite observable span; in the locked same-theory interface they must in fact be absent, or be exactly a predeclared observable renormalization. More precisely, for every finite family F_1,...,F_n in the positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, if the collar limits satisfy N(F) = lim_{delta downarrow 0} M_delta(F) = R(F)^* M(F) R(F) with R(F) invertible and compatible under restriction of finite families, then positivity of all collar matrices N(F) implies OS positivity of the intended target matrices M(F). If instead N(F)=M(F)+E(F) with a pair-dependent mixed boundary defect E(F) not representable by such a congruence, the closed-cone argument is valid only for the boundary-renormalized theory N, not for the intended continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger functions M.

assumptions: Continuum Schwinger functions are distributions on the chosen local gauge-invariant composite test space.
The reflected products of mirror-flat local composites have finite scaling degree at the reflection plane after the standard bulk composite renormalizations.
The collar maps T_delta converge to the identity in the topology of test functions with controlled jets at t=0.
definitions: Mirror-flat core: finite linear combinations of gauge-invariant local polynomial or composite fields smeared in t>0 by smooth functions whose normal jets at the reflection plane vanish to an order exceeding the distributional scaling degree of the reflected product.

Collar map T_delta: a smooth time-translation/cutoff operator sending the support of a positive-time test observable into t>=delta and converging to the identity in the test-function topology compatible with the distribution S.
Trace modulus: a bound omega_F(delta) with |S(Theta T_delta F_i · T_delta F_j)-S(Theta F_i · F_j)|<=omega_F(delta) and omega_F(delta)->0.

equations.label: local trace modulus
equations.latex: \left|S(\Theta T_\delta F_i\cdot T_\delta F_j)-S(\Theta F_i\cdot F_j)\right|\le \omega_{ij}(\delta),\qquad \omega_{ij}(\delta)\downarrow0
equations.valid_when: F_i,F_j lie in the mirror-flat local composite core and no Wilson-line/cusp singularity is present.

equations.label: core positivity limit
equations.valid_when: The trace modulus holds entrywise for the finite family F.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a local gauge-invariant composite with a reflected product whose scaling degree forces a boundary counterterm even after mirror-flat smearing; that would be a falsifier of the claimed local core trace continuity.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma separates the plausibly solved local distributional part from the genuinely nonlocal Wilson-loop obstruction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: On the mirror-flat local composite core, the trace/collar limit has no boundary defect: if F_i are gauge-invariant local composites smeared by test functions that vanish to sufficiently high order at t=0, then S(Theta T_delta F_i · T_delta F_j) converges to S(Theta F_i · F_j) by ordinary distributional continuity, so OS positivity extends from fixed collars to this core without additional Wilson-loop renormalization input.

assumptions: The suspected anomaly is visible as a multiplicative leading factor in the renormalized mixed Wilson OS entries after bulk Wilson-loop renormalization.
The four reference target entries in the 2-by-2 block are nonzero, so the ratios B_{ij}=N_{ij}/M_{ij} are meaningful.
The loops are chosen so that the only new singular geometry in the collar collapse is located at the reflection plane.
definitions: Mixed Wilson block: the finite matrix with entries S(Theta W(C_i,delta) · W(D_j,delta)) for positive-time loop families whose collars collapse toward t=0.
Individual loop renormalization: a factor z(C) assigned to each loop observable before OS pairing, producing only congruence factors overline{z(C_i)}z(D_j).
Nonfactorizing mixed defect: a boundary anomaly depending on the pair (C_i,D_j) in a way that has nonzero 2-by-2 multiplicative curvature B_{11}B_{22}-B_{12}B_{21}.

equations.label: mixed anomaly ratio
equations.valid_when: Both numerator and denominator are defined after the same bulk Wilson-loop renormalization and the denominator is nonzero.

equations.label: 2-by-2 nonfactorization witness
equations.valid_when: A nonzero Delta_B proves that no individual factors z(C),z(D) can account for the boundary anomaly on this block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit a hairpin or cusp family for which Delta_B is nonzero after all allowed bulk and individual Wilson-loop renormalizations.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This gives an experimentally checkable falsifier for the same-theory bridge in the Wilson sector.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A practical Wilson-loop obstruction test is the mixed-cusp 2-by-2 minor test: for collar-approximated Wilson loops C_i,D_j whose reflected products approach the reflection plane, any multiplicative anomaly B(C_i,D_j) that fails the rank-one identities B_{11}B_{22}=B_{12}B_{21} on a finite OS block is a nonfactorizing mixed defect and cannot be removed by individual loop renormalizations.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot only if a mixed Wilson cusp or boundary-contact computation produces a nonfactorizing defect that cannot be absorbed by the locked observable renormalization.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves, for a dense Wilson-loop core, that every reflected collar OS matrix has trace limit equal to the target matrix or to a compatible invertible congruence fixed before cutoff removal.
control_decision.reason: The branch is still productive: it has reduced an abstract topology question to a precise finite-matrix factorization/no-defect theorem and a concrete Wilson-loop falsifier test.

dependency_updates.description: The bridge now has two layers: fixed-collar closed-cone transfer, which is formal and valid under reflected-probe convergence, and a nonformal finite-matrix trace/congruence theorem at the reflection plane.
The algebra must be locked before the trace limit. Any boundary-renormalized Wilson product added after collar collapse changes the theory, even if the resulting OS matrices are positive.

The topology must control fixed-collar reflected OS entries and provide enough uniformity or trace modulus to identify the delta downarrow 0 matrix limit with the intended target matrix up to allowed congruence.

falsifiers: A concrete mixed Wilson block with anomaly ratios B_{ij} satisfying B_{11}B_{22} != B_{12}B_{21}; this is a falsifier because no individual loop renormalization can turn the collar-positive matrix into the intended target OS matrix by congruence.

A reflected hairpin family whose cusp anomalous factor depends on the pair of loops rather than on each loop separately, producing an additive or multiplicative matrix defect E(F) that is not compatible under restriction of finite families.
A boundary contact term supported at t=0 in the product Theta W(C_delta) · W(D_delta) that survives the delta downarrow 0 limit and is not part of the predeclared continuum Schwinger functional.
A cutoff-removal topology that is valid for fixed collars but not uniform enough to take the trace limit over the finite OS matrix entries.
An observable-algebra change in which boundary-renormalized Wilson products are silently added; this may preserve reflection positivity but is a falsifier of the same-theory condition.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 181 converts the Wilson obstruction into a finite-dimensional linear algebra criterion. The closed-cone passage proves positivity for the collar limit N, but the intended target M inherits positivity only if the boundary trace defect is zero or an invertible congruence already built into the same theory. This yields a sharp falsifier: a nonfactorizing mixed Wilson anomaly detected by a nonzero 2-by-2 multiplicative minor. The local mirror-flat sector still looks valid by distributional continuity, so the remaining hard Yang-Mills estimate is specifically a finite OS-matrix no-new-boundary-renormalization theorem for reflected Wilson products.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out a 2-by-2 mixed Wilson block for mirror-symmetric hairpin/cusp loop families approaching t=0. Compute or bound the anomaly ratios B_{ij}; test whether the rank-one identity B_{11}B_{22}=B_{12}B_{21} is forced by locality/multiplicative renormalization or can fail through a genuine pair-dependent boundary contact.
